walkthroughs.body_html:
Landscape Systems, Processes & Change (Coastal / Glaciated) — a core area of A-Level Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Landscape Systems, Processes & Change (Coastal / Glaciated) brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Landscape Systems, Processes & Change (Coastal / Glaciated).

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is the enhanced greenhouse effect?
options: Sea level rises because of underwater volcanoes pushing it up.
The strengthening of the natural greenhouse effect by human activities (mainly burning fossil fuels) which add CO2 and other gases to the atmosphere.
It is the hole in the ozone layer letting in more sun.
The greenhouse effect is entirely man-made and harmful.

mcqs.q: What causes global sea level rise?
options: Two main factors: thermal expansion of warming seawater, and the melting of land-based ice (glaciers and ice sheets) adding water to oceans.
Climate change only happens in summer.
Sea level rises because of underwater volcanoes pushing it up.
Sea level rises mainly because Arctic sea ice is melting.

mcqs.q: Why can a cold winter NOT disprove climate change?
options: It is the hole in the ozone layer letting in more sun.
Climate change only happens in summer.
A really cold winter proves global warming is not happening.
Climate is the long-term statistical average; a single cold winter is a weather event. Climate change is the trend in averages and extremes over decades, not the absence of cold days.
